model.name: UAV printed sleeve dipole (867 MHz)
model.description: Printed sleeve dipole on a slim vertical FR-4 strip (1.6 mm, board in the xz plane, z up), with no ground plane, for a UAV with a non-metal (composite) fuselage. The upper arm is a copper strip; the lower arm is the sleeve, a pair of strips either side of the coax, joined to the coax braid by a bridge at their top. The coax is modelled as a strip (its outer conductor) from the bridge down to the bottom edge of the board, where the cable leaves. A 50 ohm lumped port across the feed gap g stands for the coax inner conductor jumping from the braid to the upper arm. Vertically polarised and omnidirectional in azimuth for the 863-870 MHz SRD / LoRa band, with the best match at about 877 MHz (1.1 % high) so that a glass-fibre radome pulls it into the band. Its tuning, its results and how to scale it to other bands are described with the example designs in the Fairbeam documentation.
